title: Correct gravitational acceleration
description: Essential: The final expression for g must be exactly g = 2 * h * v_0^2 / (x^2 - h^2).

title: Correct first cosmic velocity
description: Essential: The final expression for the first cosmic velocity must be exactly v = v_0 * sqrt(2 * h * R / (x^2 - h^2)).

title: Projectile motion analysis
description: Important: The solution must correctly derive the time of flight from the horizontal and vertical components of the projectile motion.

title: Applying Newton's Law of Gravitation
description: Important: The solution must correctly relate surface gravitational acceleration (g) to the planet's mass and radius using GM/R^2 = g.

title: Deriving cosmic velocity condition
description: Important: The solution must correctly set the gravitational force equal to the required centripetal force for a circular orbit at radius R.

title: Algebraic manipulation and substitution
description: Optional: The solution shows clear, logical steps in substituting the expression for g into the gravitational force law to eliminate M and find v.

title: Units or dimensional check
description: Optional: The solution includes a check that the final expressions for g and v have the correct physical dimensions.

title: Misidentifying horizontal displacement
description: Pitfall: Using x instead of the correct horizontal displacement sqrt(x^2 - h^2) in the projectile motion equations.

title: Sign or algebraic error
description: Pitfall: Making an algebraic mistake (e.g., incorrect exponent, sign error in x^2 - h^2) when solving for g or v.
